name: ie-cross-border
description: Use this skill when a person or company crosses the Irish border for tax. It covers the individual residence tests (183 days, or 280 days over two years with a 30-day floor), ordinary residence after three years, domicile and where the remittance basis fits, split-year treatment for employment income, the Special Assignee Relief Programme (SARP) for arrivals up to 2030 with its EUR 125,000 floor for 2026 arrivals, company residence, the 12.5% company exit tax, the CGT rule for temporary non-residents, how non-residents are taxed and the PAYE Exclusion Order, and withholding on dividends (25%), interest, patent royalties and rent paid to non-resident landlords (20%). Tax year 2026, the calendar year. Trigger on: moving to Ireland, leaving Ireland, non-resident Ireland, expat, SARP, exit tax Ireland, split year, digital nomad Ireland, DWT, A1 posting. Out of scope: ie-non-dom (remittance basis detail), ie-corporation-tax, ie-income-tax-form11, ie-cgt, ie-payroll, ie-prsi-class-s.
